papers.title_original: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address limitations in current antiviral protection methods by testing LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from human breast milk, against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including influenza A virus, to provide broad antiviral protection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the collection and purification of LCTG-001 from the breast milk of 120 lactating individuals and testing it against respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus in cell cultures and neutrophils.
analysis.methods: LCTG-001 was purified and tested for antiviral activity using cell cultures and neutrophils. The methods included SDS–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, density gradient centrifugation, and transmission electron microscopy for virus purification and quantification.
analysis.main_results: LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as novel evidence of broad antiviral protection provided by LCTG-001, which could be useful for preventing multiple respiratory viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings could inform the development of new antiviral strategies for preventing respiratory infections, particularly in vulnerable populations such as infants and the elderly.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of in vitro models and the need for further clinical validation. The evidence strength is moderate due to the in vitro nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation from human breast milk, against respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus, demonstrating broad antiviral activity. The findings suggest potential for new antiviral strategies but require further clinical validation.

papers.title_zh: 多克隆母乳来源的分泌型 IgA 赋予 抗病毒药物 广泛的针对多种呼吸道病毒的保护作用
papers.source_body_en: These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats. Approximately 1 liter of this pooled milk was processed using a previously validated and patented purification method (13) to yield a polyclonal SIgA product, designated LCTG-001. AbstractPassive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. papers.title: Bat-borne influenza A H9N2 virus shows species-specific replication and transmission
papers.abstract: Bat-borne H9N2 IAV (bat H9N2), initially detected in bat feces in Egypt in 2017, has recently attracted attention because of its unexpected pre-pandemic properties, including airborne transmission between ferrets and efficient replication in human lung explant cultures. However, its host range and potential reservoir hosts remain poorly defined, particularly with respect to additional bat hosts and mammalian or avian mixing-vessel species. Here, we compare the susceptibility of two pteropodid bat species, Rousettus aegyptiacus and Eidolon helvum, and additionally assessed pigs and quails following intranasal inoculation with bat H9N2. aegyptiacus showed only low-level viral replication and shedding, largely restricted to the upper respiratory tract, and did not show transmission to contact bats. In contrast, both juvenile and adult E. helvum, despite showing no clinical signs, showed high-level viral replication and shedding in the upper respiratory tract, with efficient and early transmission to contact bats. Viral RNA was most abundant in the respiratory turbinates, the nasopharyngeal meatus and the tracheal epithelium, where it was associated with moderate to severe necrotizing rhinitis and tracheitis. The lower respiratory tract was less involved, with viral RNA confined to scattered bronchioles and associated with focal necrotizing bronchiolitis. Other organs, including the gastrointestinal tract, lacked histologic lesions and viral RNA labeling. In pigs and quails, intranasal inoculation did not result in detectable replication, transmission, or seroconversion. Our findings demonstrate marked differences in the susceptibility to bat H9N2 between the two fruit bat species tested and identify E. helvum as a highly susceptible host capable of rapid and efficient transmission. Conversely, pigs and quails were not susceptible, suggesting that additional viral adaptations may be required to allow for a productive infection in these species.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compared the susceptibility of two pteropodid bat species, Rousettus aegyptiacus and Eidolon helvum, and also assessed pigs and quails following intranasal inoculation with bat H9N2.
analysis.methods: The researchers intranasally inoculated the animals and assessed viral replication, shedding, and transmission through examination of viral RNA levels in various tissues and observation of clinical signs.
analysis.main_results: Rousettus aegyptiacus showed only low-level viral replication and shedding, largely restricted to the upper respiratory tract, and did not show transmission to contact bats. In contrast, both juvenile and adult Eidolon helvum showed high-level viral replication and shedding in the upper respiratory tract, with efficient and early transmission to contact bats.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate marked differences in susceptibility to bat H9N2 between the two fruit bat species tested and identify Eidolon helvum as a highly susceptible host capable of rapid and efficient transmission.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the importance of understanding the host range of bat-borne H9N2 IAV for surveillance and risk assessment, particularly in identifying potential reservoir hosts and mixing-vessel species.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vivo experiments with a small number of animals and does not include long-term monitoring or broader host species, but the evidence is strong due to direct observations of replication, shedding, and transmission.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the host range and transmission potential of bat-borne H9N2 influenza A virus (IAV), which has shown unexpected pre-pandemic properties. The researchers compared the susceptibility of two fruit bat species, Rousettus aegyptiacus and Eidolon helvum, as well as pigs and quails, following intranasal inoculation. Results showed that R. aegyptiacus had low-level viral replication and no transmission, while E. helvum exhibited high-level replication and efficient transmission. These findings suggest that E. helvum may be a significant host for bat H9N2 IAV, with implications for surveillance and risk assessment. The study's limitations include a small sample size and focus on specific animal models, but the evidence is strong based on direct observations of viral behavior.

papers.title_zh: 蝙蝠传播的甲型 H9N2 流感病毒显示物种特异性复制和 传播
papers.source_body_en: Bat-borne H9N2 IAV (bat H9N2), initially detected in bat feces in Egypt in 2017, has recently attracted attention because of its unexpected pre-pandemic properties, including airborne transmission between ferrets and efficient replication in human lung explant cultures. However, its host range and potential reservoir hosts remain poorly defined, particularly with respect to additional bat hosts and mammalian or avian mixing-vessel species. Here, we compare the susceptibility of two pteropodid bat species, Rousettus aegyptiacus and Eidolon helvum, and additionally assessed pigs and quails following intranasal inoculation with bat H9N2. aegyptiacus showed only low-level viral replication and shedding, largely restricted to the upper respiratory tract, and did not show transmission to contact bats. In contrast, both juvenile and adult E. helvum, despite showing no clinical signs, showed high-level viral replication and shedding in the upper respiratory tract, with efficient and early transmission to contact bats. Viral RNA was most abundant in the respiratory turbinates, the nasopharyngeal meatus and the tracheal epithelium, where it was associated with moderate to severe necrotizing rhinitis and tracheitis. The lower respiratory tract was less involved, with viral RNA confined to scattered bronchioles and associated with focal necrotizing bronchiolitis. Other organs, including the gastrointestinal tract, lacked histologic lesions and viral RNA labeling. In pigs and quails, intranasal inoculation did not result in detectable replication, transmission, or seroconversion. Our findings demonstrate marked differences in the susceptibility to bat H9N2 between the two fruit bat species tested and identify E. helvum as a highly susceptible host capable of rapid and efficient transmission. Conversely, pigs and quails were not susceptible, suggesting that additional viral adaptations may be required to allow for a productive infection in these species.
papers.abstract_zh: 蝙蝠传播的 H9N2 IAV (bat H9N2) 最初于 2017 年在埃及的蝙蝠粪便中检测到,最近因其意想不到的大流行前特性而引起关注,包括雪貂之间的空气传播 传播 以及在人类肺外植体培养物中的有效复制。然而,其 宿主 范围和潜在的 宿主 宿主 的定义仍然不明确,特别是对于其他蝙蝠 宿主 和哺乳动物或鸟类混合容器物种。在这里,我们比较了两种翼足类蝙蝠物种 Rousettus aegyptiacus 和 Eidolon helvum 的敏感性,并另外评估了鼻内接种蝙蝠 H9N2 后的猪和鹌鹑。埃及伊蚊仅表现出低水平的病毒复制和脱落,很大程度上局限于上呼吸道,并且没有表现出传播接触蝙蝠。相比之下,幼年和成年的鼠疫,尽管没有表现出任何临床症状,但在上呼吸道中表现出高水平的病毒复制和脱落,并能有效且早期地接触蝙蝠。病毒RNA在呼吸道鼻甲、鼻咽道和气管上皮中最为丰富,与中度至重度坏死性鼻炎和气管炎有关。下呼吸道受累较少,病毒RNA局限于分散的细支气管,并与局灶性坏死性细支气管炎相关。其他器官,包括胃肠道,缺乏组织学病变和病毒 RNA 标记。在猪和鹌鹑中,鼻内接种不会导致可检测到的复制、传播 或血清转化。我们的研究结果表明,所测试的两种果蝠物种之间对蝙蝠 H9N2 的易感性存在显着差异,并将 E. helvum 鉴定为高度易感的 宿主,能够快速有效地进行 传播。相反,猪和鹌鹑不受影响,这表明可能需要额外的病毒适应才能在这些物种中产生有效的感染。

papers.title: Fitness flux in SARS-CoV-2 and influenza H3N2
papers.abstract: The tempo of viral adaptation is usually read indirectly from the composition of mutations, through measures such as dN/dS. Here we measure it directly from the dynamics of variant frequencies, where we use multinomial logistic regression to estimate a fitness for each co-circulating variant. We aggregate these estimates to derive the rate of change of mean population fitness, referred to as fitness flux. Tracing SARS-CoV-2 from its emergence, we find that it initially adapted rapidly, doubling in fitness every 6 months from Jan 2021 to Jun 2022, but slowing to every 2.4 years from Jul 2022 to Dec 2025. Seasonal influenza H3N2 sustained a slower, steadier pace doubling in fitness every 10.0 years. In both, the rate of fitness gain closely tracks the variance in fitness, matching the 1:1 expectation of Fisher’s fundamental theorem. Phylogenetic contrasts between parent and child lineages localize most fitness gain to spike, and within spike to the receptor-binding domain, where a simple count of spike S1 substitutions predicts lineage fitness about as well as deep-learning escape and protein-language-model scores. Measuring fitness directly thus offers a transparent, frequency-based alternative to mutational proxies for tracking and anticipating viral adaptation. The website blab.github.io/fitness-flux/ is the intended reading experience of this paper, providing responsive layout and interactive figures.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study investigates the tempo of viral adaptation in seasonal influenza viruses, focusing on the rate of fitness gain and its relationship to mutation accumulation. It compares SARS-CoV-2 and influenza H3N2, with a specific emphasis on tracking fitness flux through variant frequency dynamics.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review employs a direct method to measure fitness flux by analyzing variant frequency dynamics using multinomial logistic regression. This approach estimates fitness for each co-circulating variant and aggregates these to calculate the rate of change of mean population fitness.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study finds that SARS-CoV-2 initially adapted rapidly, doubling in fitness every 6 months from Jan 2021 to Jun 2022, but this rate slowed to every 2.4 years from Jul 2022 to Dec 2025. In contrast, seasonal influenza H3N2 sustained a slower, steadier pace, doubling in fitness every 10.0 years. The rate of fitness gain in both viruses closely tracks the variance in fitness, aligning with the 1:1 expectation of Fisher’s fundamental theorem.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study notes that while the rate of fitness gain matches Fisher’s theorem, the specific regions of the genome contributing to fitness changes remain under investigation. The analysis localizes most fitness gain to the spike protein, particularly the receptor-binding domain, but the exact mechanisms and the role of other genomic regions are not fully resolved.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The direct measurement of fitness flux offers a transparent, frequency-based alternative to mutational proxies for tracking and anticipating viral adaptation. This method could inform surveillance strategies, vaccine development, and public health interventions by providing a clearer understanding of how viral fitness evolves over time.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the tempo of viral adaptation in seasonal influenza viruses, comparing SARS-CoV-2 and influenza H3N2. It introduces a direct method to measure fitness flux using variant frequency dynamics and multinomial logistic regression. The findings reveal that SARS-CoV-2 initially adapted rapidly, doubling in fitness every 6 months, but this rate slowed to every 2.4 years after 2022. In contrast, seasonal influenza H3N2 showed a slower, steadier adaptation pace, doubling in fitness every 10 years. The study highlights that fitness gain closely tracks variance in fitness, aligning with Fisher’s fundamental theorem. It also identifies the spike protein, particularly the receptor-binding domain, as a key region for fitness changes. The research suggests that direct fitness measurement could improve surveillance and public health responses to viral evolution.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述采用直接方法通过使用多项逻辑回归分析变频动态来测量适应通量。这种方法估计每个共同循环变体的适应度,并将它们聚合起来以计算平均群体适应度的变化率。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究调查了 季节性流感 病毒的病毒适应节奏,重点关注适应度增益率及其与 季节性流感 积累的关系。它比较了 SARS-CoV-2 和流感 H3N2,特别强调通过变异频率动态跟踪健康流量。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述采用直接方法通过使用多项逻辑回归分析变频动态来测量适应通量。这种方法估计每个共同循环变体的适应度,并将它们聚合起来以计算平均群体适应度的变化率。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,SARS-CoV-2 最初适应速度很快,从 2021 年 1 月到 2022 年 6 月,适应度每 6 个月翻一番,但从 2022 年 7 月到 2025 年 12 月,这一速度放缓至每 2.4 年一次。相比之下,季节性流感 H3N2 保持了更慢、更稳定的速度,每 10.0 年适应度翻一番。两种病毒的适应度增益率密切跟踪适应度的方差,与费舍尔基本定理的 1:1 期望一致。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究指出,虽然适应度增益率符合费舍尔定理,但 基因组 导致适应度变化的特定区域仍在调查中。该分析将大部分适应性增益定位于刺突蛋白,特别是受体结合域,但其他基因组区域的确切机制和作用尚未完全解决。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 适应通量的直接测量为突变代理提供了一种透明的、基于频率的替代方案,用于跟踪和预测病毒适应。该方法可以通过更清楚地了解病毒适应度如何随时间演变而为 监测 策略、疫苗 开发和公共卫生干预措施提供信息。

papers.title: Lineage Dynamics and Risk Factors Underlying Serotype 4 Invasive Pneumococcal Disease in Spain.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The emergence of vaccine-covered serotypes causing invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) is a serious concern worldwide. METHODS: We characterized all national serotype 4 IPD isolates from children and adults received at the Spanish Pneumococcal Reference Laboratory (2009-2024). RESULTS: We investigated the unexpected rise of serotype 4 causing IPD in young adults after the COVID-19 pandemic, affecting the elderly population in recent years. Epidemiological and genomic analysis confirmed that the rise started as an abrupt cluster of cases in Seville (Andalusia) in the year 2022 due to the ST15063 within the GPSC12 lineage. This outbreak initially affected nonvaccinated young individuals associated with high rates of tobacco smoking, alcohol, and inhaled drugs followed by a general distribution through the country in the following years that affected adults ≥65 years old. Moreover, ST15063 serotype 4 strains displayed enhanced infection rates of human lung cells that significantly increased in the presence of cigarette smoke exposure and by influenza A(H3N2) coinfection. CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the need for targeted vaccination strategies, molecular surveillance, and focused interventions in high-risk populations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the rise of serotype 4 invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) in Spain, particularly in young adults after the COVID-19 pandemic. The research focuses on the epidemiological and genomic characteristics of the ST15063 lineage within the GPSC12 group, which was identified as the cause of an abrupt cluster of cases in Seville in 2022. The outbreak initially affected nonvaccinated young individuals with high rates of tobacco smoking, alcohol, and inhaled drug use, followed by a broader distribution affecting adults aged ≥65 years. The study also found that these strains showed increased infection rates in human lung cells, especially under cigarette smoke exposure and influenza A(H3N2) coinfection. The authors emphasize the importance of targeted vaccination strategies, molecular surveillance, and interventions in high-risk populations. The evidence is based on isolates from the Spanish Pneumococcal Reference Laboratory between 2009 and 2024, and the findings are interpreted as highlighting the need for focused public health measures. The study's limitations include its focus on serotype 4 IPD and the absence of detailed statistical or laboratory procedures.

papers.title: Disruption of the polyuracil tract can greatly enhance immunostimulatory properties of influenza delVGs
papers.abstract: Non-standard viral genomes (nsVGs) are replication-incompetent genomes within viral populations whose presence has been associated with an enhanced immune response. This association has garnered interest in their use as potential antivirals, vaccine adjuvants, or general immune-modulators. In influenza A virus (IAV), the predominant nsVG is a large deletion in one of the three polymerase segments, which results in deletion-containing viral genomes (delVGs). Work from our group has found that individual delVGs can be recovered that are capable of stimulating high levels of interferon, however we and others have not previously found any consistent means of predicting or modifying determinants of this stimulation. Using high-throughput genetic approaches, we find that specific mutations disrupting the polyuracil tract in IAV delVGs can enhance interferon production by up to two orders of magnitude. Such variants can also associate with improved rescue in artificial systems engineered to exclude infectious virus, and can greatly suppress the growth of replication-competent virus. These findings indicate the polyuracil tract is a key, and unexpected, target for improvement of immunostimulatory delVGs derived from IAV.

papers.title: Evolutionary reconstruction of bat influenza A viruses reveals segment-specific histories and host-associated selection
papers.abstract: Abstract Influenza A (IAV) is a major zoonotic pathogen infecting a broad range of vertebrate hosts. In this study, we focus on inferring the evolutionary history of a subset of novel IAV, isolated from New World bats, which use a non-canonical host receptor and infer their relationship to sialic-acid-binding IAV. Little is known about when these novel subtypes emerged and how selection has acted upon them compared to sialic-acid-binding circulating strains. The current state of the field is split on whether bats are natural reservoirs for a distinct yet low abundance IAV lineage, or if influenza underwent rapid evolution after a recent spillover from a species within its standard host range. By analyzing segment-specific phylogenies, we hope to clarify the evolutionary history of bat IAV. Our objectives are to infer the date of divergence of non-canonical bat IAV from sialic-acid binding IAV, identify patterns of selection acting on bat IAV compared to representative samples of sialic-acid-binding IAV to identify potential signatures of genome-wide adaptation, and finally to reconstruct ancestral state transitions to infer which host taxa preceded spillover into bats. To accomplish this, we analyzed each IAV genome segment independently using least-squares molecular dating, Bayesian discrete-trait ancestral host reconstruction, and branch-site selection tests. Our results suggest that non-canonical bat IAV diverged from major IAV lineages 100-200 years ago, supporting a deeper evolutionary history rather than a very recent spillover event. However, discordance among genome segments in inferred divergence times, selective pressures, and ancestral hosts indicates that bat IAV experienced segment-specific evolutionary histories. Together, these findings suggest that non-canonical bat IAV represents a deeply divergent lineage with a complex evolutionary history involving segment-specific selection and host-transition dynamics.

The research aims to clarify whether these bat IAVs represent a deeply divergent lineage or a recent spillover event. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项研究中,我们重点推断从新大陆蝙蝠中分离出来的新型 IAV 子集的进化史,这些 IAV 使用非规范的 宿主 受体,并推断它们与唾液酸结合 IAV 的关系。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 甲型流感 (IAV) 是一种主要的人畜共患病原体,感染多种脊椎动物 宿主。在这项研究中,我们重点推断从新大陆蝙蝠中分离出来的新型 IAV 子集的进化史,这些 IAV 使用非规范的 宿主 受体,并推断它们与唾液酸结合 IAV 的关系。与唾液酸结合的循环菌株相比,人们对这些新亚型何时出现以及选择如何作用于它们知之甚少。该领域目前的状态存在分歧,即蝙蝠是否是天然的 储存宿主(针对独特但低丰度的 IAV 谱系),或者流感是否在最近来自其标准 宿主 范围内的物种的 跨物种溢出 后经历了快速 进化。通过分析特定片段的系统发育,我们希望阐明蝙蝠 IAV 的进化历史。我们的目标是推断非规范蝙蝠 IAV 与唾液酸结合 IAV 的分歧日期,与唾液酸结合 IAV 的代表性样本相比,识别作用于蝙蝠 IAV 的选择模式,以确定 基因组 广泛适应的潜在特征,最后重建祖先状态转换以推断哪个 宿主 分类单元先于 跨物种溢出 进入蝙蝠。为了实现这一目标,我们使用最小二乘分子测年、贝叶斯离散特征祖先 宿主 重建和分支位点选择测试独立分析了每个 IAV 基因组 片段。我们的结果表明,非典型蝙蝠 IAV 在 100-200 年前就与主要 IAV 谱系分离,支持了更深层的进化历史,而不是最近的 跨物种溢出 事件。然而,基因组 片段之间在推断的分歧时间、选择压力和祖先 宿主 方面的不一致表明,蝙蝠 IAV 经历了片段特异性的进化历史。总之,这些发现表明,非典型蝙蝠 IAV 代表了一个截然不同的谱系,具有复杂的进化历史,涉及片段特异性选择和 宿主 过渡动力学。

papers.title: Mixed Pneumonia with Pulmonary Embolism and Multiple Pathogens Detected in Bronchoalveolar Lavage Fluid: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Severe community-acquired pneumonia may involve mixed pathogens and concurrent vascular complications. A 72-year-old man presented with fever, nonproductive cough, vomiting, hypoxemia, markedly elevated inflammatory markers, and an elevated D-dimer concentration. Chest computed tomography showed left lower-lobe consolidation and pleural effusion. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography, obtained because of hypoxemia and suspected pulmonary embolism, showed a filling defect in a right upper-lobe pulmonary artery. The patient received antimicrobial therapy prior to bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL). Bronchoscopy was performed in the bronchopulmonary segment corresponding to the radiographic lesion, and approximately 10 mL of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) was recovered aseptically for microbiological and cytological testing. An aliquot of at least 3 mL was allocated to a multiplex pathogen-targeted sequencing assay, which detected Chlamydia psittaci, influenza A H3N2, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and additional conditionally pathogenic or commensal organisms. The three principal detections were interpreted in conjunction with the clinical presentation, imaging, inflammatory markers, BALF cytology, conventional testing, and treatment response. The patient improved during antimicrobial and anticoagulant treatment and was discharged on December 3, 2025. At the documented outpatient follow-up on December 17, rivaroxaban was continued for approximately one further month. This case highlights the adjunctive value and interpretive limitations of targeted sequencing in a treated patient. The serial imaging and invasive sampling reflected case-specific decisions and should not be interpreted as a routine protocol for pneumonia.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对一名 72 岁男性进行了 病例报告 治疗,该男性出现发烧、干咳、呕吐、低氧血症、炎症标志物显着升高以及 D-二聚体浓度升高。该研究涉及连续成像和侵入性采样,以评估临床表现和诊断结果。
elements_zh.methods: 将至少 3 mL 的支气管肺泡灌洗液 (BALF) 等分试样分配给多重病原体靶向测序测定。该检测检测到了鹦鹉热衣原体、甲型H3N2流感、肺炎链球菌和其他条件致病性或共生生物。
elements_zh.main_results: 计算机断层扫描肺血管造影显示右上叶肺动脉充盈缺损。靶向测序分析确定甲型 H3N2 流感、鹦鹉热衣原体和肺炎链球菌为三种主要病原体。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果结合临床表现、影像学、炎症标志物、BALF 细胞学、常规测试和 治疗 反应进行解释。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该病例强调了考虑重症肺炎混合病原体的重要性以及靶向测序在识别多种病原体方面的价值。它还强调在复杂的临床情况下需要综合诊断方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于单个 病例报告,这限制了普遍性。连续成像和侵入性采样反映了针对具体病例的决定,不应被解释为肺炎的常规方案。

papers.title: Matrix Metalloproteinase-8 Deficiency Alters the Balance Between Viral Clearance and Immunopathology in H1N1 Infection.
papers.abstract: Matrix metalloproteinase-8 (MMP-8) regulates inflammatory responses, but its contributions to the pathogenesis of influenza A viral (IAV) disease are not known. Plasma MMP-8 levels were increased 30-fold in subjects infected with H1N1 or seasonal IAV and were inversely associated with the PaO2/FiO2 ratio, suggesting potential value as a candidate marker of lung injury severity that requires validation in larger cohorts. MMP-8 levels were elevated in the lungs of H1N1-infected wild-type (WT) mice and localized to airway epithelial cells, macrophages, and polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNs). H1N1-infected Mmp-8-/- mice exhibited lower mortality and reduced lung viral burdens, but developed more severe lung injury than WT mice. Gene expression profiling revealed enhanced necroptosis and an exaggerated immune response in the lungs of infected Mmp-8-/- mice. Infected Mmp-8-/- mice had increased airway epithelial necroptosis with higher pulmonary levels of Type I interferons (IFNs), and increased frequencies of Class II MHC molecule-expressing macrophages and CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, and higher levels of some Th1 cytokines. In vitro, MMP-8 cleaved IL-1β and IL-6, but not Type I IFNs. These findings suggest that Mmp-8 deficiency is associated with restricted influenza virus spread and increased lung injury, accompanied by enhanced Type I IFN-associated necroptotic signaling and augmented antiviral immune responses. The latter may partly involve loss of MMP-8-mediated processing of pro-inflammatory mediators. MMP-8 may represent a host-response target in severe influenza infection, although therapeutic strategies targeting MMP-8 will need to balance enhanced viral clearance against the risk of increased lung immunopathology.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 基质金属蛋白酶 8 (MMP-8) 调节炎症反应,但其对甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 疾病 发病机制 的贡献尚不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及感染 H1N1 的野生型 (WT) 小鼠和 Mmp-8-/- 小鼠,测量了感染 H1N1 或季节性 IAV 的受试者的血浆 MMP-8 水平。
elements_zh.methods: 感染 H1N1 的 WT 小鼠肺部 MMP-8 水平升高,并定位于气道上皮细胞、巨噬细胞和多形核中性粒细胞 (PMN)。
elements_zh.main_results: H1N1 感染的 Mmp-8-/- 小鼠表现出较低的 死亡率 和肺部病毒负荷减少,但比 WT 小鼠出现更严重的肺损伤。基因表达谱显示,受感染的 Mmp-8-/- 小鼠肺部坏死性凋亡增强,免疫应答 增强。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 受感染的 Mmp-8-/- 小鼠气道上皮坏死性凋亡增加,肺部 I 型干扰素 (IFN) 水平升高,表达 II 类 MHC 分子的巨噬细胞和 CD4+ 和 CD8+ T 细胞的频率增加,以及一些 Th1 细胞因子水平升高。MMP-8 可能代表严重流感感染中的 宿主 反应靶标,尽管针对 MMP-8 的治疗策略需要在增强的病毒清除率与增加的肺部免疫病理学风险之间取得平衡。

papers.title: Protective Effects of Influenza B Neuraminidase Antibodies Against Symptomatic Influenza Virus Infection.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza vaccines are designed to induce hemagglutinin-inhibiting (HAI) antibodies rather than neuraminidase-inhibiting (NAI) antibodies; therefore, NAI antibodies' protective effects need further investigation. Neuraminidase-inhibiting antibodies' protective effects, independent of HAI antibodies, have been demonstrated for influenza A viruses, but not influenza B viruses (IBVs). METHODS: Employing H6NB reassortant virus targets, we evaluated NAI antibodies' protective effects against IBV in sera from a prospective influenza vaccine effectiveness study among healthcare personnel (HCP) in Israel. Antibody titers against B/Brisbane/60/2008 and B/Phuket/3073/2013 were quantified by HAI and NAI assays. Matched NAI and HAI antibody titers from baseline and postvaccination sera were analyzed for the 2017-2018 influenza season. RESULTS: Laboratory-confirmed IBV infection was recorded in 64/262 HCP and influenza vaccination in 187/262 HCP. Vaccination did not consistently elicit rising NAI titers against vaccine strain B/Brisbane, with a geometric mean fold rise of 1.1 (95% CI: .9-1.3). However, comparing baseline NAI titers, geometric mean titer ratios were 1.50 (95% CI: 1.0-2.1) times higher against B/Brisbane and 2.5 (95% CI: 1.7-3.6) times higher against circulating B/Phuket in vaccinated versus unvaccinated HCP. Each 2-fold rise in NAI antibody titers reduced the hazard of symptomatic infection by 42% (95% CI: 36%-48%) against B/Phuket and 23% (95% CI: 13%-33%) against B/Brisbane, adjusting for HAI titers. CONCLUSIONS: Neuraminidase-inhibiting antibodies were a strong correlate of protection against symptomatic IBV infection, with protective effects independent of those from HAI antibodies. These findings suggest that the use and standardization of neuraminidase content in influenza vaccines could provide broader protection against influenza.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the protective effects of neuraminidase-inhibiting (NAI) antibodies against symptomatic influenza B virus (IBV) infection, highlighting a gap in current vaccine design that focuses on hemagglutinin-inhibiting (HAI) antibodies. The research was conducted among healthcare personnel (HCP) in Israel using sera from a prospective vaccine effectiveness study. NAI and HAI antibody titers were quantified against specific IBV strains, and the results showed that NAI titers were significantly higher in vaccinated HCP compared to unvaccinated individuals. The study found that each 2-fold increase in NAI titers reduced the risk of symptomatic infection by 42% against B/Phuket and 23% against B/Brisbane, independent of HAI titers. These findings suggest that NAI antibodies could be a strong correlate of protection against IBV, potentially offering broader protection if incorporated into influenza vaccines. However, the study's results are limited to the 2017-2018 season and focus on a specific population, which may affect generalizability.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:流感疫苗疫苗旨在诱导血凝素抑制(HAI)抗体,而非神经氨酸酶抑制(NAI)抗体;因此,需要进一步研究NAI抗体的保护作用。对于流感A病毒,神经氨酸酶抑制抗体的保护作用已被证明,但尚未在流感B病毒(IBVs)中得到证实。方法:我们采用H6NB重配病毒作为靶标,在以色列的医疗工作者(HCP)中进行前瞻性流感疫苗接种有效性研究,评估NAI抗体对IBV的保护作用。通过HAI和NAI试验定量测定针对B/Brisbane/60/2008和B/Phuket/3073/2013的抗体滴度。分析了2017-2018流感季节基线和疫苗接种后血清中匹配的NAI和HAI抗体滴度。结果:实验室确认的IBV感染在64/262名HCP中被记录,而流感疫苗接种感染在187/262名HCP中被记录。疫苗接种并未一致诱导针对疫苗株B/Brisbane的NAI滴度上升,几何均数滴度上升为1.1(95% CI:.9-1.3)。然而,与未接种疫苗的HCP相比,接种疫苗的HCP针对B/Brisbane的基线NAI滴度几何均数滴度比为1.50(95% CI:1.0-2.1),针对流行B/Phuket的几何均数滴度比为2.5(95% CI:1.7-3.6)。在调整HAI滴度后,针对B/Phuket的NAI抗体滴度每上升2倍,症状性感染的危险性降低42%(95% CI:36%-48%),针对B/Brisbane的危险性降低23%(95% CI:13%-33%)。结论:神经氨酸酶抑制抗体是针对症状性IBV感染的强保护相关因素,其保护作用独立于血凝素抑制抗体的作用。这些发现表明,在流感疫苗中使用和标准化神经氨酸酶成分可能提供更广泛的流感保护。

papers.title: Immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine in adults living with HIV compared with HIV-uninfected adults: a study from China
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) in adults aged ≥18 years living with HIV and to provide evidence supporting influenza vaccination in this population in China. Methods This single-center, open-label comparative analysis was derived from a larger three-arm clinical study. For the present comparative analysis, 472 vaccinated participants were planned, including 236 adults living with HIV (Group 1) and 236 age- and sex-comparable HIV-uninfected adults (Group 2). Participants in both groups received one dose of IIV3 (0.5 mL) on Day 0. Blood samples were collected before and 28 days after vaccination for hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody testing against A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria strains. Immunogenicity endpoints included seroconversion rate, seroprotection rate, geometric mean titer (GMT), and geometric mean increase (GMI). Safety was assessed by monitoring solicited and unsolicited adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) during 6 months of follow-up. An unvaccinated cohort of adults living with HIV from the original trial was included only for an exploratory, descriptive analysis of influenza-like illness (ILI), without assessment of vaccine efficacy. Results A total of 489 participants were enrolled, including 237 in Group 1 and 252 in Group 2. At 28 days post-vaccination, seroconversion rates did not differ significantly between Group 1 and Group 2 for A(H1N1) (91.00% vs. 86.69%, P > 0.05), but significantly lower for A(H3N2) (49.50% vs. 89.52%) and B/Victoria (40.00% vs. 64.52%) (both P < 0.001). Seroprotection rates were also lower in Group 1 than in Group 2 for A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria (94.00% vs. 97.18%, and 40.50% vs. 68.55%, respectively). Post-vaccination GMTs were significantly lower in Group 1 for all three strains (all P < 0.001). GMI was higher for A(H1N1) but lower for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in Group 1 than in Group 2 (all P < 0.001). Multivariable analyses showed that HIV infection remained independently associated with several measures of vaccine-induced immune responses after adjustment for demographic and clinical factors, particularly for A(H3N2). IIV3 was generally safe and well tolerated. Most AEs were mild in severity, and no Grade 4 adverse reactions or vaccine-related SAEs were reported. During the period from 29 days to 6 months after vaccination, few influenza-like illness events were reported among vaccinated and unvaccinated participants living with HIV; these findings were descriptive and were not used to assess vaccine efficacy against influenza. Conclusion Adults living with HIV developed substantial antibody responses following IIV3 vaccination, although the magnitude of response varied across influenza strains. A(H1N1) seroconversion was high in adults living with HIV, whereas responses to A(H3N2) and B/Victoria were generally lower than those in HIV-uninfected adults. HIV infection remained associated with reduced vaccine-induced immune responses for several strain-specific outcomes after multivariable adjustment, with associations particularly evident for A(H3N2). IIV3 was safe and well tolerated, supporting current recommendations for influenza vaccination in adults living with HIV. Clinical trial registration https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=255613 , identifier ChiCTR2500112191.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-center, open-label comparative analysis was derived from a larger three-arm clinical study. It included 472 vaccinated participants, with 236 adults living with HIV (Group 1) and 236 age- and sex-comparable HIV-uninfected adults (Group 2).
analysis.methods: Blood samples were collected before and 28 days after vaccination for hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody testing against A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria strains. Safety was assessed by monitoring solicited and unsolicited adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) during 6 months of follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) in adults living with HIV compared to HIV-uninfected adults in China. The research aimed to provide evidence for influenza vaccination in this population. A total of 489 participants were enrolled, with 237 in the HIV group and 252 in the uninfected group. At 28 days post-vaccination, seroconversion rates for A(H1N1) were similar between groups, but significantly lower for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in the HIV group. HIV infection was independently associated with reduced immune responses to A(H3N2) after multivariable adjustment. The vaccine was generally safe and well tolerated, with most adverse events being mild. The study was a single-center analysis, which may limit generalizability, and the evidence is moderate due to the observational design and potential confounding factors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估三价灭活流感 疫苗 (IIV3) 在成人 HIV 感染者中的免疫原性和安全性,并为中国该人群中流感 疫苗 的支持提供证据。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在多变量调整后,HIV 感染与 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 减少独立相关,对于几种毒株特异性结果,甲型H3N2流感病毒 的关联尤其明显。

papers.title_zh: 与未感染 HIV 的成人相比,三价灭活流感 疫苗 对 HIV 感染者的免疫原性和安全性:来自中国的一项研究
papers.source_body_en: Objective To evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) in adults aged ≥18 years living with HIV and to provide evidence supporting influenza vaccination in this population in China. Methods This single-center, open-label comparative analysis was derived from a larger three-arm clinical study. For the present comparative analysis, 472 vaccinated participants were planned, including 236 adults living with HIV (Group 1) and 236 age- and sex-comparable HIV-uninfected adults (Group 2). Participants in both groups received one dose of IIV3 (0.5 mL) on Day 0. Blood samples were collected before and 28 days after vaccination for hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody testing against A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria strains. Immunogenicity endpoints included seroconversion rate, seroprotection rate, geometric mean titer (GMT), and geometric mean increase (GMI). Safety was assessed by monitoring solicited and unsolicited adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) during 6 months of follow-up. An unvaccinated cohort of adults living with HIV from the original trial was included only for an exploratory, descriptive analysis of influenza-like illness (ILI), without assessment of vaccine efficacy. Results A total of 489 participants were enrolled, including 237 in Group 1 and 252 in Group 2. At 28 days post-vaccination, seroconversion rates did not differ significantly between Group 1 and Group 2 for A(H1N1) (91.00% vs. 86.69%, P > 0.05), but significantly lower for A(H3N2) (49.50% vs. 89.52%) and B/Victoria (40.00% vs. 64.52%) (both P < 0.001). Seroprotection rates were also lower in Group 1 than in Group 2 for A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria (94.00% vs. 97.18%, and 40.50% vs. 68.55%, respectively). Post-vaccination GMTs were significantly lower in Group 1 for all three strains (all P < 0.001). GMI was higher for A(H1N1) but lower for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in Group 1 than in Group 2 (all P < 0.001). Multivariable analyses showed that HIV infection remained independently associated with several measures of vaccine-induced immune responses after adjustment for demographic and clinical factors, particularly for A(H3N2). IIV3 was generally safe and well tolerated. Most AEs were mild in severity, and no Grade 4 adverse reactions or vaccine-related SAEs were reported. During the period from 29 days to 6 months after vaccination, few influenza-like illness events were reported among vaccinated and unvaccinated participants living with HIV; these findings were descriptive and were not used to assess vaccine efficacy against influenza. Conclusion Adults living with HIV developed substantial antibody responses following IIV3 vaccination, although the magnitude of response varied across influenza strains. A(H1N1) seroconversion was high in adults living with HIV, whereas responses to A(H3N2) and B/Victoria were generally lower than those in HIV-uninfected adults. HIV infection remained associated with reduced vaccine-induced immune responses for several strain-specific outcomes after multivariable adjustment, with associations particularly evident for A(H3N2). IIV3 was safe and well tolerated, supporting current recommendations for influenza vaccination in adults living with HIV. Clinical trial registration https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=255613 , identifier ChiCTR2500112191.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的 评价三价灭活流感 疫苗 (IIV3) 在中国 18 岁以上成人 HIV 感染者中的免疫原性和安全性,为中国该人群感染 疫苗 流感提供证据。方法 这项单中心、开放标签的比较分析源自一项更大规模的三组临床研究。在本次比较分析中,计划有 472 名接种疫苗的参与者,其中包括 236 名感染艾滋病毒的成年人(第 1 组)和 236 名年龄和性别相当的未感染艾滋病毒的成年人(第 2 组)。两组参与者均在第 0 天接受一剂 IIV3 (0.5 mL)。在 疫苗接种 之前和之后 28 天收集血样,用于针对 A(H1N1)、甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 毒株的血凝抑制 (HI) 抗体测试。免疫原性终点包括血清转化率、血清保护率、几何平均滴度(GMT)和几何平均增加(GMI)。通过在 6 个月的随访期间监测主动和主动不良事件 (AE) 以及严重不良事件 (SAE) 来评估安全性。原始试验中未接种疫苗的 队列研究 成人 HIV 感染者仅用于对流感样疾病 (ILI) 进行探索性、描述性分析,未评估 疫苗 的疗效。结果 共有 489 名参与者入组,其中第 1 组 237 名,第 2 组 252 名。疫苗接种 后 28 天,A(H1N1) 组 1 和组 2 之间的血清转换率没有显着差异(91.00% vs. 86.69%,P > 0.05),但 甲型H3N2流感病毒 的血清转换率显着较低(49.50% 对比 89.52%)和 B/维多利亚(40.00% 对比 64.52%)(均 P < 0.001)。A(H1N1)、甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 的血清保护率在第 1 组中也低于第 2 组(分别为 94.00% vs. 97.18% 和 40.50% vs. 68.55%)。第 1 组中所有三种菌株的 疫苗接种 后 GMT 均显着较低(所有 P < 0.001)。第 1 组中 A(H1N1) 的 GMI 较高,但 甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 的 GMI 低于第 2 组(所有 P < 0.001)。多变量分析表明,在调整人口和临床因素(特别是 甲型H3N2流感病毒)后,HIV 感染仍然与 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 的多项测量值独立相关。IIV3 通常是安全且耐受性良好的。大多数 AE 的严重程度较轻,没有报告 4 级不良反应或 疫苗 相关的 SAE。在 疫苗接种 后 29 天至 6 个月期间,接种疫苗和未接种疫苗的 HIV 感染者中几乎没有报告流感样疾病事件;这些发现是描述性的,并不用于评估 疫苗 对流感的功效。结论 成人 HIV 感染者在 IIV3 疫苗接种 后产生了显着的抗体反应,尽管反应的程度因流感毒株而异。在感染 HIV 的成年人中,A(H1N1) 血清转化率较高,而对 甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 的反应通常低于未感染 HIV 的成年人。在多变量调整后,HIV 感染仍然与 疫苗 诱导的 免疫应答 减少有关,对于几种毒株特异性结果,甲型H3N2流感病毒 的关联尤其明显。IIV3 安全且耐受性良好,支持当前针对成人 HIV 感染者流感 疫苗接种 的建议。临床试验注册https://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=255613,标识符ChiCTR2500112191。

papers.title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
papers.abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk-derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from human breast milk, as a passive immunization strategy against respiratory viruses. The research addresses the limitations of current approaches, which rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies. The study demonstrates that LCTG-001 has broad antiviral activity against respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus, including H5N1. papers.title: Parental Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Toward Influenza Vaccine Uptake Among Children in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background: Seasonal influenza is a major public health concern, particularly among children who are at high risk of infection and can transmit the virus to others. Vaccination is the primary preventive measure. Parental knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) may influence vaccination decisions. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among Saudi parents attending primary healthcare centers in Jeddah. Parents with at least one child aged six months or older were eligible. Data were collected using a validated self-administered Arabic questionnaire assessing knowledge, attitudes, awareness, perceived barriers, and vaccine uptake. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to examine associations, and binary logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of vaccine uptake. Results: A total of 308 parents participated. Influenza vaccine uptake was reported by 57.5% of participants. Nearly all participants (97.7%) demonstrated good knowledge, but the knowledge score was not significantly associated with vaccine uptake (p = 0.399). Parental attitude was a significant independent predictor (OR = 1.090, 95% CI: 1.033-1.149, p = 0.001). Education level was also significantly associated with uptake (p = 0.015), with lower-educated parents showing higher odds of vaccination compared to postgraduate-educated parents. Exposure to awareness campaigns was significantly associated with higher uptake (p < 0.001). The most reported barriers were the belief that vaccination was unnecessary (9.4%) and concerns about side effects (8.4%), both strongly associated with non-vaccination (p < 0.001). Conclusion: Although most parents had good knowledge about influenza vaccination, this did not translate into consistent vaccination behavior. Parental attitudes and awareness campaign exposure were the main predictors of vaccine uptake. Public health strategies should shift from broad factual dissemination to targeted, point-of-care counseling that addresses misconceptions about vaccine necessity and safety to improve influenza vaccination rates among children in Saudi Arabia.

papers.full_text: AbstractObjectivesTo analyze the epidemiological characteristics of six common respiratory pathogens in cases of Acute Respiratory Tract Infection (ARTI) in Hangzhou from 2018 to 2025, to provide a basis for clinical diagnosis and treatment, as well as public health prevention and control.MethodsA multicenter retrospective study was conducted. Data from 81,974 ARTI cases from seven medical institutions in Hangzhou City between January 2018 and December 2025 were collected. Cases with positive test results were analyzed for influenza A virus (FluA), influenza B virus (FluB), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), adenovirus (ADV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP), and Chlamydia pneumoniae (CP), and statistical analysis was performed according to the pandemic stage, age, sex, season, and co-infection status.ResultsAmong 81,974 patients, a total of 33,350 cases tested positive for pathogens, with an overall positive rate of 40.68%. MP (19.56%) and FluA (16.93%) were the most prevalent pathogens. The positivity rates of each pathogen showed statistically significant differences across the three stages before, during, and after the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic (all P < 0.001). Compared with the pre-COVID-19 pandemic period (2018–2019), the positive rates of FluA, FluB, and MP were significantly suppressed during the COVID-19 pandemic period (2020–2022), and then experienced a sharp “revenge rebound” in the post-COVID-19 pandemic period (2023–2025) (for example, the positive rate of MP rebounded from 5.43% to 21.09%). In contrast, the positive rates of RSV, ADV, and CP showed a persistent state of inhibition, but the absolute number of cases far exceeded that of before the COVID-19 pandemic. MP had the highest infection rate among 6– < 12 years old (38.31%), whereas FluA was more common in adults. The epidemiological distribution showed obvious seasonal heterogeneity: FluA/FluB/RSV were more prevalent in winter, MP was active in autumn, and ADV was more prevalent in summer. The co-infection rate was 7.22% (5,922 cases), and the most common combination was FluA + MP, accounting for 53.82% of all co-infections.ConclusionFrom 2018 to 2025, the pathogen spectrum of ARTI in Hangzhou was mainly composed of MP and FluA. The COVID-19 pandemic and related non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) have had a profound and heterogeneous impact on the epidemic pattern of respiratory pathogens. FluA, FluB, and MP showed the characteristics of “suppression-retaliatory rebound.” In the post-COVID-19 pandemic era, the activity of pathogens has clear seasonal, age, and gender distribution patterns, and the rate of mixed infections is high. The research results suggest that a dynamic monitoring system needs to be established, and targeted prevention and control measures should be implemented for key individuals and pathogens during high-incidence seasons.Keywords: Acute Respiratory Tract Infection, epidemiological characteristics, Hangzhou, influenza virus, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, pathogen spectrum 2.Materials and methods2.1.Study populationThis study aimed to systematically characterize the epidemiological features of six key respiratory pathogens—influenza A virus (FluA), influenza B virus (FluB), RSV, adenovirus (ADV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP), and Chlamydia pneumoniae (CP)—among ARTI cases in Hangzhou, and to evaluate the long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on local pathogen dynamics. A total of 81,974 patients from seven medical institutions in Hangzhou seven medical institutions in Hangzhou (see Supplementary Table 1 for details) between January 2018 and December 2025 were selected as study subjects. The diagnostic criteria for cases were as follows: pediatric cases were defined according to the Practical Pediatrics (Zhu Futang, 8th edition) (8), while adult cases were defined according to the Expert consensus on the diagnosis, treatment, and infection control of acute respiratory infections in adult outpatient and emergency departments (9), including: (1) Upper respiratory tract infection (URTI): presence of ≥2 symptoms—fever (body temperature ≥38 °C), cough, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, sore throat, or sneezing—with a duration of ≤ 7 days. (2) Lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI): Clinical signs: increased respiratory rate, moist rales/whistling sounds in the lungs, or tracheal retractions; Radiological evidence (X-ray/CT): signs of pneumonia/bronchitis (e.g., patchy infiltrates, atelectasis). Exclusion criteria: Incomplete clinical data, incomplete pathogen detection results, or duplicate records. Clinical data from 1,431,696 individuals undergoing respiratory pathogen screening were collected in this study. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, we excluded entries with incomplete pathogen detection, removed duplicate data from repeated hospitalizations and repeated outpatient visits (1,331,565 cases), as well as duplicate data between outpatient and inpatient records (18,157 cases). Ultimately, a total of 81,974 subjects were included in the statistical analysis (Figure 1).Figure 1Flowchart of the study.Flowchart illustrating a retrospective study design, showing data collection from seven medical institutions, inclusion and exclusion criteria, cohort selection process, analysis dimensions, and six key epidemiological outcomes for respiratory pathogen infections.2.2.Data collectionDemographic and clinical data of enrolled cases were collected through the “Xiaoshan Health Data Platform” platform. The determination of infection status was based on any of the following positive test results: positive serum pathogen-specific IgM antibodies, or positive pathogen antigens or nucleic acids detected in respiratory tract samples. This study encompasses six common respiratory pathogens, including FluA, FluB, RSV, ADV, MP, and CP. For all six pathogens, specimen types included nasopharyngeal or oropharyngeal swabs, sputum, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, and blood; detection methods included serological IgM assays, antigen detection, and nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT), with the exception that antigen detection was not included for CP. Positivity criteria followed the manufacturers' instructions for each respective assay. Only patients with complete test results for all six target pathogens were included in the final analysis.Grouping of study subjects: in accordance with the World Health Organization (WHO) criteria for age-stage division and population age stratification, the study subjects were divided into six age groups: 0– < 3 years (infant and toddler group), 3– < 6 years (preschool group), 6– < 12 years (school-age group), 12– < 18 years (adolescence group), 18– < 60 years (adult group), and ≥60 years (older adult(s) group). According to year span, the subjects were divided into three periods: 2018–2019, 2020–2022, and 2023–2025. Seasonal grouping included spring (March–May), summer (June–August), autumn (September–November), and winter (December–February of the following year). The chi-square (χ2) two-sided test was used for intergroup comparisons of qualitative data, and a P-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.2.3.Statistical analysisData were exported to Excel, and statistical analyses were performed using R version 4.3.2. Normally distributed continuous data are presented as mean ± standard deviation, while non-normally distributed data are presented as median (interquartile range, IQR). Positivity rates for each study period were calculated as the total number of positive cases divided by the total number of tested cases across all years within that period. Count data are presented as frequencies and percentages. Comparisons between groups were performed using the chi-square test. All tests were two-sided, and the significance level was set at α = 0.05. Calculation formula: Positive rate (%) = (Number of positive cases detected among the screened population / Total number of screened cases) × 100%. Supplementary materialThe Supplementary Material for this article can be found online at: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1907370/full#supplementary-material Supplementary Materials 3.Results3.1.Basic characteristics of the research subjectsAmong 81,974 patients with ARTI, 33,350 were positive for pathogens, with a positivity rate of 40.68%. Specifically, the positive rate for outpatient cases was 44.64% (30,405/68,109), and that for inpatient cases was 19.83% (2,749/13,865). Among the 81,974 ARTI patients screened from 2018 to 2025, the number of cases each year was 1,915, 3,116, 1,086, 1,676, 2,963, 19,630, 31,639, and 19,949, respectively. The pathogen positive rates were 21.78% (417/1,915), 26.03% (811/3,116), 14.09% (153/1,086), 10.80% (181/1,676), 14.21% (421/2,963), 51.08% (10,027/19,630), 39.03% (12,350/31,639), and 44.08% (8,794/19,949), respectively, as shown in Figure 2. There were 41,996 males and 39,978 females, with a male-to-female ratio of 1.05:1. The median age was 24.00 (5.00, 37.00) years.Figure 2The number and positive rate of respiratory pathogens in acute respiratory infection cases in Hangzhou from 2018 to 2025.Stacked bar and line chart showing annual positive cases of a disease in outpatients and hospitalized patients from 2018 to 2025, with positive rates peaking in 2023 and 2024 before declining in 2025.Further stratified analysis revealed significant variations in the outpatient-inpatient positivity gap across subgroups (Supplementary Table 2). By age, the largest disparity was observed in children aged 3– < 6 years, with a positivity rate of 59.50% in outpatients compared to 22.44% in inpatients (difference of 36.9 percentage points). By time period, the gap widened markedly in the post-COVID-19 pandemic period (2023–2025: 51.27% vs. 22.93%) compared to the pre-COVID-19 pandemic period (2018–2019: 35.18% vs. 23.57%). By pathogen, Flu A, Flu B, and MP showed higher positivity in outpatients, whereas RSV, ADV, and CP were higher in inpatients.3.2.Analysis of the positive detection status of pathogens and their temporal trendsFrom 2018 to 2025, among the acute respiratory infection cases in Hangzhou, the detection results of six common respiratory pathogens showed that MP had the highest overall positive rate (19.56%, 16,035/81,974), followed by FluA (16.93%, 13,876/81,974). The overall positivity rates of the remaining four pathogens ranged from 0.23% to 7.25%, including FluB (7.25%, 5,946/81,974), RSV (2.45%, 2,007/81,974), ADV (1.85%, 1,518/81,974), and CP (0.23%, 190/81,974).Chi-square tests were performed to assess overall differences in the positive rates of each pathogen across the three period. The results indicated that the differences in the positive rates of each pathogen among the three periods were significant (all P < 0.001). Specifically, the positive rates of FluA, MP, and FluB showed a suppression during the COVID-19 pandemic period and rebounded significantly after the pandemic, presenting a typical “revenge-style epidemic” pattern, whereas, the positive rates of RSV, ADV, and CP showed a persistent state of inhibition, but the absolute number of cases was substantially higher than before the pandemic. The positive rates of MP and FluA from 2020 to 2022 demonstrated a decrease compared to 2018–2019 and from 2023 to 2025, showing an obvious “V-shaped” trend. Among them, the positive rate of MP during the COVID-19 pandemic period (5.43%) decreased by 61.1% compared with that before the pandemic (13.95%), and rebounded to 21.09% after the pandemic, an increase of 288.3% compared with the COVID-19 pandemic period; the positive rate of FluA during the COVID-19 pandemic period (1.57%) decreased by 58.5% compared with that before the pandemic (3.78%), and increased to 19.09% after the pandemic, an increase of 1115.9% compared with the COVID-19 pandemic period. The positive rates of ADV and CP from 2018 to 2019 were higher than those from 2020 to 2022 and from 2023 to 2025. The positive rate of ADV was 5.39% before the pandemic and decreased to 1.55% and 1.63% in the latter two periods, respectively; the positive rate of CP was 1.19% before the pandemic and decreased to 0.05% and 0.18% in the latter two periods, respectively. The positive rates of RSV were 3.08%, 2.90%, and 2.37% in the three periods, respectively, showing a gradual downward trend (P < 0.001). It is worth noting that although the overall positive rate decreased, the number of cases in the post-COVID-19 pandemic period (2023–2025) (1,686 cases) was much higher than that before the pandemic (155 cases), suggesting an increase in the absolute number of infected individuals (Table 1 and Figure 3).Table 1Comparison of positive rates of respiratory pathogen antibodies in different time periods.Pathogens2018–2019 year (N = 5,031)2020–2022 year (N = 5,725)2023–2025 year (N = 71,218)χ2 valueP-valueFlu A190 (3.78)90 (1.57)13,596 (19.09)1815.708< 0.001Flu B79 (1.57)135 (2.36)5,732 (8.05)512.402< 0.001RSV155 (3.08)166 (2.90)1,686 (2.37)15.263< 0.001ADV271 (5.39)89 (1.55)1,158 (1.63)368.627< 0.001MP702 (13.95)311 (5.43)15,022 (21.09)933.074< 0.001CP60 (1.19)3 (0.05)127 (0.18)217.617< 0.001Data are presented as N (%). Positivity rates for each study period were calculated as the total number of positive cases divided by the total number of tested cases across all years within that period. χ2 values were derived from 3 (time periods) × 2 (positive/negative) contingency tables for each pathogen independently. Total positive rate was defined as the proportion of cases testing positive for at least one of the six target pathogens. FluA, influenza A virus; FluB, influenza B virus; RSV, respiratory syncytial virus; ADV, adenovirus; MP, Mycoplasma pneumoniae; CP, Chlamydia pneumoniae.Figure 3Monthly positive rate trends of six respiratory pathogens in Hangzhou, 2018–2025. FluA, influenza A virus; FluB, influenza B virus; RSV, respiratory syncytial virus; ADV, adenovirus; MP, Mycoplasma pneumoniae; CP, Chlamydia pneumoniae.Line graph showing positive rates by year from 2018 to 2025 for six respiratory viruses: FluA, FluB, RSV, ADV, MP, and CP. Sections are marked as pre-pandemic (2018-2019), pandemic control (2020-2022), and post-pandemic (2023-2025). MP and FluA rates spike sharply after 2023, while all virus rates drop markedly during the pandemic control period.Upon further analysis of seasonal trends, the total positive detection rate of respiratory pathogens exhibited a fluctuating upward trend across seasons (χ2 = 3335.18, P < 0.001), indicating significant overall seasonal variation. However, pathogen-specific seasonal differences were not uniform: most pathogens showed statistically significant seasonal variation (P < 0.05), while CP exhibited no significant seasonal difference. Specifically, FluA, FluB, and RSV shared a winter-peaking pattern, with the highest positive rates in winter (21.90%, 10.87%, and 2.76%, respectively) and the lowest in summer or autumn. ADV peaked in summer (3.28%) and troughed in winter (1.19%), while MP peaked in autumn (21.62%) and troughed in spring (14.49%). CP showed consistently low positivity across all seasons (0.22%−0.26%), with no statistically significant differences. The overall positive detection rate of respiratory pathogens in male patients was 39.52% (15,798/39,978), and that in female patients was 41.79% (17,552/41,996). Comparisons of positive rates between genders were performed separately for each pathogen and for the overall positivity using chi-square tests. full_text_sections.discussion: 4.DiscussionThis study conducts a multi-center retrospective analysis of a total of 81,974 ARTI cases in Hangzhou from 2018 to 2025, describing the temporal variations in the epidemic patterns of six major respiratory pathogens before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Our data confirm the rebound phenomenon of pathogen activity observed globally in the post-COVID-19 pandemic era. However, the recovery patterns varied markedly across pathogens: Flu A and MP rebounded rapidly to pre- COVID-19 pandemic levels, whereas RSV and ADV exhibited delayed or incomplete recovery. These divergent trajectories resulted in a reshaped epidemiological landscape, characterized by altered seasonal peaks and shifts in the age groups predominantly affected. These findings have important implications for understanding the complexity of the “immunity debt” hypothesis, optimizing clinical practice, and reconstructing the local surveillance and early-warning system.Research findings indicate that there are significant differences in the inhibitory effects of NPIs on common respiratory pathogens. The positive rates of Influenza A (FluA), Influenza B (FluB), and MP were significantly suppressed during the period of epidemic prevention and control from 2020 to 2022, and then showed a sharp “revenge rebound” from 2023 to 2025. In particular, the positive rate of FluA in the post-COVID-19 pandemic period (19.09%) was more than five times that before the COVID-19 pandemic (3.78%), representing a rebound increase of over 11-fold compared with the COVID-19 pandemic period (1.57%). This phenomenon is consistent with reports from many countries around the world and is widely attributed to the “immunity debt,” that is, NPIs led to a decrease in natural infections among the population and an accumulation of susceptible individuals. Once the interventions were lifted, the pathogens spread rapidly among the population with immunity gaps (7, 10, 11).However, the decline in the positive rates of ADV, CP, and RSV in this study challenges the view that the single “immune debt” hypothesis can universally explain the dynamics of all pathogens, and reveals the “asymmetry” of the impact of NPIs (12). This disparity is the result of the combined effects of pathogen characteristics, population immunodynamics, and persistent changes in behavioral patterns after the pandemic. Taking ADV as an example, it has multiple transmission routes such as droplet, fecal-oral, and contact (13), this niche breadth may have buffered the impact of NPIs, preventing the complete interruption of its transmission during the pandemic and thus avoiding the accumulation of a large susceptible population like that of influenza viruses and MP (14). The latter two are highly dependent on droplet transmission and are strongly suppressed under NPIs, which in turn leads to a “revenge epidemic” after the lifting of the interventions. It is worth noting that the interpretation of the “decline in the positive rate” requires extra caution. Although the positive rates of ADV, CP, and RSV show a persistent state of inhibition, the absolute number of detected cases during the post-COVID-19 pandemic period (2023–2025) far exceeds the pre-COVID-19 pandemic level (15–17). This strongly suggests that the simple positive rate may underestimate the actual intensity of community transmission and disease burden of this pathogen in the post-COVID-19 pandemic stage. The reasons for this phenomenon may include: the recovery and increase in the overall number of medical consultations after the pandemic, the improvement in the willingness to undergo testing, and the sample dilution effect caused by the co-circulation with other pathogens (such as MP, FluA) (18, 19). Therefore, our data indicate that the evolution of respiratory pathogens in the “post-pandemic era” is not simply a “return to the baseline,” but rather a profound “restructuring of ecological niches.” With their high transmission efficiency, MP and influenza viruses have significantly increased their epidemiological weight in the context of expanded susceptible pools and the restoration of transmission conditions; while other pathogens have their activity levels reshaped either due to their transmission characteristics or because of sustained behavioral suppression (20). This suggests that in the surveillance during the “post-COVID-19 pandemic era,” it is necessary to combine multi-dimensional indicators such as the positive rate and the absolute number of cases, and take into account confounding factors such as changes in medical seeking behavior to more accurately assess the real epidemic situation and disease burden of various pathogens.The stratified outpatient-inpatient comparison further illustrates how healthcare-seeking behavior shapes surveillance data. The universal lower inpatient positivity rate across age groups likely reflects that inpatients include more non-infectious admissions and prior antibiotic use. The widening gap post- COVID-19 pandemic suggests a surge in mild community infections seeking outpatient care. Notably, RSV and ADV were higher in inpatients, consistent with their tendency to cause more severe disease requiring hospitalization (21, 22).This study clearly identifies that MP has become the pathogen with the highest positive rate (19.56%) among ARTI cases in the Hangzhou area, far exceeding that of FluA (16.93%). Age distribution analysis showed that MP infection peaked in children aged 6– < 12 years (38.31%), consistent with recent reports from multiple domestic regions (23, 24). The higher overall positivity of MP compared to RSV in our cohort reflects their distinct age-specific ecological niches rather than diminished clinical relevance of RSV. Age-stratified analysis (Table 4) revealed that MP positivity increased markedly with age, peaking in school-aged children (6– < 12 years: 38.31%), whereas RSV activity was concentrated in infants and toddlers (< 3 years: 5.30%). In older age groups, MP positivity far exceeded RSV (e.g., 6– < 12 years: 38.31% vs. 0.82%), which explains why MP appears more prevalent in the all-ages cohort. RSV remains a critical pathogen causing severe lower respiratory tract infections predominantly in young children, and its importance should not be underestimated despite the lower overall positivity rate in this study. The high susceptibility of 6– < 12 years old can be explained by aspects such as their group living characteristics, immune system development features, and social behavior traits. As semi-enclosed and high-density environments, schools provide ideal conditions for the transmission of MP through droplets. Meanwhile, since children's immune systems are not fully developed and their specific immune memory of MP is relatively limited, these factors collectively make this population the primary victims of MP infection (25).In addition, research has found that the mixed infection pattern (accounting for 17.8% of the total positive cases) provides important clues for understanding the severity of the disease. FluA + MP is the most predominant co-infection combination (accounting for 53.82% of all multiple infections), and this phenomenon deserves high-level attention. Basic research suggests that influenza virus infection can damage respiratory epithelial cells and disrupt the function of the mucosal barrier, thereby creating favorable conditions for the secondary colonization and infection of pathogens such as MP (26). Clinically, co-infection of influenza and mycoplasma may be associated with a longer fever duration, a higher risk of pulmonary imaging progression, and more complex treatment decisions (27). Our data indicate that such co-infections are more prevalent in winter, coinciding with the influenza season. This suggests that during the influenza season, for patients diagnosed with influenza, especially child patients, the possibility of MP co-infection should be vigilant to avoid missed diagnos…
full_text_sections.other: 1.IntroductionAcute Respiratory Tract Infection (ARTI) is a leading cause of outpatient visits and emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and substantial disease burden globally. The pathogen spectrum of ARTI is complex and encompasses viruses, bacteria, and atypical pathogens (1). In China, ARTI is a prevalent infectious disease, which can lead to severe clinical consequences, especially among children, the older adult(s), and individuals with underlying diseases (2). Clarifying the epidemic characteristics of pathogens in specific periods and regions holds crucial scientific value for guiding empirical clinical treatment, implementing precise public health intervention measures (such as vaccination and seasonal prevention), and establishing effective monitoring and early warning systems.In recent years, the epidemic patterns of respiratory pathogens have changed. The global pandemic of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) that began at the end of 2019, along with the widespread implementation of Non-Pharmaceutical Interventions (NPIs) to contain its spread, such as wearing masks, maintaining social distancing, and restricting gatherings and travel, have profoundly altered the ecological and epidemiological characteristics of common respiratory pathogens (3). Multiple studies have confirmed that during the strict implementation of NPIs, the activity levels of many common respiratory viruses, such as influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), significantly decreased or even disappeared (4, 5). However, since the gradual adjustment and lifting of NPIs at the end of 2022, new trends have emerged in many parts of the world, including the resurgence of common respiratory pathogen activities, shift in epidemic seasons, and co-circulation or alternating prevalence of multiple pathogen (6). For example, post-COVID-19 pandemic surveillance in Guangdong Province revealed that the peak activity of influenza viruses has advanced, the proportion of MP infections has exceeded the pre-COVID-19 pandemic average, and there are significant age-related differences in pathogen distribution (7). These changes indicate that in the “post-COVID-19 pandemic era,” the original pathogen prevalence patterns based on historical data may no longer be applicable, and there is an urgent need for updates and analyses based on the latest monitoring data.As an important central city and transportation hub in eastern China, Hangzhou has a dense population and high population mobility, making it an ideal sentinel site for monitoring the dynamics of respiratory infectious disease. However, there is currently a lack of systematic, long-term longitudinal research covering the complete cycle before the COVID-19 pandemic, during thepandemic, and after the implementation of “Category B Management for Category B Infectious Diseases” on the epidemiological characteristics of multiple pathogens among ARTI cases in Hangzhou, especially studies that simultaneously cover viruses and atypical pathogens. To address this gap, we conducted a multicenter retrospective study of 81,974 ARTI cases from seven hospitals in Hangzhou (2018–2025) to systematically characterize the epidemiological dynamics of six common respiratory pathogens before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. 2.1.Study populationThis study aimed to systematically characterize the epidemiological features of six key respiratory pathogens—influenza A virus (FluA), influenza B virus (FluB), RSV, adenovirus (ADV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP), and Chlamydia pneumoniae (CP)—among ARTI cases in Hangzhou, and to evaluate the long-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on local pathogen dynamics. A total of 81,974 patients from seven medical institutions in Hangzhou seven medical institutions in Hangzhou (see Supplementary Table 1 for details) between January 2018 and December 2025 were selected as study subjects. The diagnostic criteria for cases were as follows: pediatric cases were defined according to the Practical Pediatrics (Zhu Futang, 8th edition) (8), while adult cases were defined according to the Expert consensus on the diagnosis, treatment, and infection control of acute respiratory infections in adult outpatient and emergency departments (9), including: (1) Upper respiratory tract infection (URTI): presence of ≥2 symptoms—fever (body temperature ≥38 °C), cough, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, sore throat, or sneezing—with a duration of ≤ 7 days. (2) Lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI): Clinical signs: increased respiratory rate, moist rales/whistling sounds in the lungs, or tracheal retractions; Radiological evidence (X-ray/CT): signs of pneumonia/bronchitis (e.g., patchy infiltrates, atelectasis). Exclusion criteria: Incomplete clinical data, incomplete pathogen detection results, or duplicate records. Clinical data from 1,431,696 individuals undergoing respiratory pathogen screening were collected in this study. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, we excluded entries with incomplete pathogen detection, removed duplicate data from repeated hospitalizations and repeated outpatient visits (1,331,565 cases), as well as duplicate data between outpatient and inpatient records (18,157 cases). Ultimately, a total of 81,974 subjects were included in the statistical analysis (Figure 1).Figure 1Flowchart of the study.Flowchart illustrating a retrospective study design, showing data collection from seven medical institutions, inclusion and exclusion criteria, cohort selection process, analysis dimensions, and six key epidemiological outcomes for respiratory pathogen infections. 2.2.Data collectionDemographic and clinical data of enrolled cases were collected through the “Xiaoshan Health Data Platform” platform. The determination of infection status was based on any of the following positive test results: positive serum pathogen-specific IgM antibodies, or positive pathogen antigens or nucleic acids detected in respiratory tract samples. This study encompasses six common respiratory pathogens, including FluA, FluB, RSV, ADV, MP, and CP. For all six pathogens, specimen types included nasopharyngeal or oropharyngeal swabs, sputum, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, and blood; detection methods included serological IgM assays, antigen detection, and nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT), with the exception that antigen detection was not included for CP. Positivity criteria followed the manufacturers' instructions for each respective assay. Only patients with complete test results for all six target pathogens were included in the final analysis.Grouping of study subjects: in accordance with the World Health Organization (WHO) criteria for age-stage division and population age stratification, the study subjects were divided into six age groups: 0– < 3 years (infant and toddler group), 3– < 6 years (preschool group), 6– < 12 years (school-age group), 12– < 18 years (adolescence group), 18– < 60 years (adult group), and ≥60 years (older adult(s) group). According to year span, the subjects were divided into three periods: 2018–2019, 2020–2022, and 2023–2025. Seasonal grouping included spring (March–May), summer (June–August), autumn (September–November), and winter (December–February of the following year). The chi-square (χ2) two-sided test was used for intergroup comparisons of qualitative data, and a P-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. 2.3.Statistical analysisData were exported to Excel, and statistical analyses were performed using R version 4.3.2.
